2608.27049.title: Research Design Tracking and Assessment for the Social Sciences
2608.27049.paper_summary: Reliable assessment of causal research designs in the social sciences is critical for evidence-based policy-making, yet has so far relied entirely on manual expert analysis. We introduce Automated Research Design Tracking and Assessment (ARDTrA), a task that involves detecting the research design used in a paper and assessing the quality of its application. We create an expert-annotated dataset of papers covering six families of counterfactual research designs and evaluate the task using a multi-turn RAG-based conversational pipeline. Across four retrieval strategies, four LLMs and six embedding models, we find that passage length is the main driver of performance, explaining 52-66% of the variance. A per-research-design analysis also shows that human and machine difficulty do not align: the designs that prove hardest for the system are not those on which expert annotators disagree most, pointing to two independent sources of task difficulty.
2608.27049.paper_summary_zh: 可靠評估社會科學中的因果研究設計對於基於證據的政策制定至關重要，但迄今為止完全依賴人工專家分析。我們介紹自動化研究設計追蹤與評估（ARDTrA），這是一項涉及檢測論文中使用的研究設計並評估其應用質量的任務。我們創建了一個專家標註的數據集，涵蓋六類反事實研究設計，並使用基於多輪RAG的對話管道來評估該任務。在四種檢索策略、四個大型語言模型和六個嵌入模型中，我們發現段落長度是性能的主要驅動因素，解釋了52-66%的變異性。每種研究設計的分析也顯示人類和機器的難度並不一致：系統最難處理的設計並不是專家標註者最有分歧的設計，這指向了任務難度的兩個獨立來源。
